scenario.symptoms: Riders reported two drivers arriving for the same trip during surge. Support logs show two ACCEPT transitions on one ride id within 200 ms in different regions.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Dispatch uses read-modify-write on ride status in SQL without row-level locking or compare-and-set. Mobile retries race on accept.

incident.headline: Concurrent accept requests assign multiple drivers to one ride

agenda.goal: Ensure exactly one driver wins assignment for a given ride.
agenda.opener: Two drivers were dispatched for one trip—what concurrency bug allowed that?

evidence.strong: Optimistic locking on ride version, single-row UPDATE … WHERE status=REQUESTED, idempotent accept tokens, and transactional outbox to notify loser.
evidence.adequate: Application-level mutex on one server only.
evidence.weak: Last accept wins without checking prior assignee.

misconceptions.pattern: Assuming mobile taps are naturally serialized.
misconceptions.challenge: Two drivers tap accept within milliseconds—what does the database see?

probes: Write the SQL or CAS operation for accept.
How do you notify the losing driver?
hints: State machine transitions must be atomic.
agenda.referenceFix: Atomic UPDATE ride SET driver_id=?, status=ASSIGNED WHERE id=? AND status=REQUESTED; if 0 rows, reject second accept and push ride taken event to loser.

scenario.symptoms: Riders waited 12 minutes while the app showed three drivers ‘2 min away’. Those drivers had gone offline or moved neighborhoods; location index TTL was 5 minutes with 30s update interval.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Geo index stores last ping without availability flag coupling. Offline events are processed asynchronously.

incident.headline: Geo index retains offline drivers with outdated locations

agenda.goal: Show only available drivers with fresh locations.
agenda.opener: App showed nearby drivers who were not actually there—how should the geo index stay accurate?

evidence.strong: Short TTL on geo cells, heartbeat + availability bit, remove on offline event, verify with dispatch lock before confirm ETA.
evidence.adequate: Longer ping interval without TTL eviction.

probes: What happens if driver app loses network mid-ride?
How fresh must location be for ETA quotes?
hints: Geo entry should include available flag.
agenda.referenceFix: Store driver_id with lat/lon, available flag, and timestamp; evict after 60–90s without ping; on match, revalidate availability before presenting ETA.

nuggets.title: Surge pricing stuck after event ends

scenario.symptoms: After a stadium concert, surge multiplier stayed at 3.5x for 90 minutes in a geohash that no longer had demand. Drivers avoided the area while riders still saw high prices.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Surge computed on 15-minute sliding demand/supply ratio without decay when supply returns; geohash granularity too coarse.

incident.headline: Surge multipliers fail to decay after localized demand spike ends

agenda.goal: Localize surge to real-time supply/demand imbalance.
agenda.opener: Surge stayed high long after the concert crowd left—what would you fix in pricing signals?

evidence.strong: Finer geohashes, exponential decay on multiplier, cap ramp-down speed, blend supply online counts, and manual ops override hooks.
evidence.adequate: Shorter window but same coarse cells.

probes: How do you prevent surge oscillation?
What inputs besides ride requests matter?
agenda.referenceFix: Recompute surge every minute on fine geohashes with decay toward 1.0 when supply/demand ratio normalizes, and expose staleness timestamp to clients.
